key_insight: Elastic frontogenesis creates thin polymer-stress sheets whose amplification during thinning sets broadband spectra even when the velocity field remains spatially smooth.
engineering_relevance: This mechanism could guide the interpretation and modeling of low-inertia polymer flows where elastic stresses drive complex motion.
method: Identify polymer-stress sheets stretched in-plane and compressed across their thickness.
Relate sheet amplification and thinning to the polymer conformation spectrum.
Use the Stokes response to connect this geometric scaling to velocity spectra.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports robust power-law spectra in velocity and polymer conformation, but provides no quantitative results or evaluation details.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify the parameter ranges or validation needed to establish applicability across viscoelastic flow models.
paper_title: Elastic frontogenesis sets the spectra of smooth elastic turbulence
